edges.reason: The destination parameter is the callee of the low-level call; a signature-approved malicious contract destination can re-enter submit.
The value parameter is forwarded as msg.value to the external destination, enabling fund movement during reentry.
Arbitrary calldata from the signature payload is forwarded to the destination contract.
tx.origin is hashed into the signed payload, tying authorization to a specific externally owned account.
msg.sender is recorded in the Deposit event when ETH is received.
onlyOwner compares the caller (msg.sender via _msgSender) against _owner.
onlyAdministrator resolves msg.sender through isAdministrator before allowing execution.
isAdministrator reads the administrators mapping for the tested address.
renounceOwnership clears the _owner state variable.
transferOwnership overwrites the _owner state variable.
submit requires the initialized flag, preventing execution on an uninitialized instance.
requiredSignatures bounds the signature verification loop in submit.
submit increments nonce with an unchecked addition under Solidity 0.6 semantics.
submit calls safeRecover once per required signature.
safeRecover invokes the ecrecover precompile to derive the signer address.
The recovered address is used by submit for owner and uniqueness checks.
addAdmin is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
removeAdmin is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
renounceOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
The stored logic address is packed into the proxy creation code by createLiteSig.
createLiteSig deploys the Proxy creation code, running its constructor.
createLiteSig performs the CREATE2 deployment inside inline assembly.
The factory immediately calls init on the freshly deployed LiteSig; init itself is publicly callable and uninitialized instances can be front-run.
The Proxy fallback delegatecalls into the logic contract address stored in the proxy slot.
The Proxy constructor writes the logic address into PROXIABLE_SLOT using assembly sstore.
The factory constructor self-registers the deployer as an administrator.
_msgSender returns msg.sender, which feeds the ownership and administrator checks.
A malicious destination can call back into submit during the low-level call, before callers observe the final state.

normalization_plan.reason: destination is the direct callee argument of the low-level call and only matters as input to that unsafe operation.
value is forwarded verbatim as msg.value of the low-level call and has no independent state effect.
data is the raw calldata of the low-level call and is fully absorbed by that unsafe operation.
recovered exists only inside the submit loop to verify ownersMap membership and ordering.
success only selects the Execution/ExecutionFailure event emitted by submit.
_owners is only consumed by init to populate owners and ownersMap.
_requiredSignatures is only stored into the requiredSignatures state variable by init.
chainId is only used by init when computing the EIP712 domain separator.
salt is used only as the CREATE2 salt within createLiteSig.
deployedAddress holds the create2 result and is used only for the init call and return.
code is the temporary bytecode buffer consumed by createLiteSig's assembly block.
hash is the sole payload passed to the ecrecover operation inside safeRecover.
